pfleeger.title: Software Engineering: Theory and Practice
pfleeger.authors: Shari Lawrence Pfleeger and Joanne M. Atlee

software-process-and-life-cycle.read: Chapter 2: Modeling the Process and Life Cycle
software-process-and-life-cycle.why: The lecture's meaning of process, its characteristics and the reasons for modelling follow this chapter.

waterfall-and-v-models.read: Chapter 2, Section 2.2: Software Process Models (waterfall, V model, prototyping)
waterfall-and-v-models.why: The waterfall, waterfall-with-prototype and V models as in the lecture.

prototyping-phased-and-spiral-models.why: Increments and iterations, production and development systems, and Boehm's spiral.

agile-rad-and-choosing-a-process.why: The agile manifesto, agile practices and when to use plan-driven or agile approaches.

requirements-and-modelling-notations.read: Chapters 4 and 5: Requirements Engineering; System Modeling
requirements-and-modelling-notations.why: Functional and non-functional requirements, use case, sequence, class and state diagrams.

dependability-and-formal-methods.read: Chapters 10 and 12: Dependable Systems; Safety Engineering (formal methods)
dependability-and-formal-methods.why: Critical systems, the dimensions of dependability and the role of formal methods.

testing-quality-and-maintenance.read: Chapters 8, 9 and 24: Software Testing; Software Evolution; Quality Management
testing-quality-and-maintenance.why: Development, release and user testing, maintenance and Lehman's laws, and quality assurance.
